title: Dhurandhar: The Revenge Soundtrack Submitted for Grammy Consideration
excerpt: T-Series and B62 Studios have mounted a Grammy consideration campaign for Shashwat Sachdev's 14-track album, entered in the Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media category among eight categories. A submission is the first step in the process — it is not a nomination.
body:
• T-Series and B62 Studios have entered Shashwat Sachdev's 14-track Dhurandhar: The Revenge album into the Grammy Awards consideration race, credited under Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media among eight categories, per Times Now and Inshorts.
  • Eight songs anchor the campaign: "Phir Se," "Jaan Se Guzarte Hai," "Kanhaiyya," "Aari Aari," "Jaiye Sajana," "Destiny – Mann Atkeya," "Vaari Jaavan" and "Hum Pyaar Karne Wale."
  • A submission is only the first step — it buys a spot on the ballot; nominations are decided by Recording Academy voting members who whittle thousands of entries down to the final shortlist.
  • The move follows the Film Federation of India jury snubbing Dhurandhar for India's official Oscar submission, making the Grammys an alternate route to global recognition.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=NHk7scrb_9I

The music of Dhurandhar: The Revenge is headed to Los Angeles. T-Series and B62 Studios have entered Shashwat Sachdev's 14-track soundtrack for the Ranveer Singh spy epic into the Grammy Awards consideration race,. The submission — the first step in a long process, not a nomination — puts one of Indian cinema's biggest recent scores in contention on the industry's biggest stage.

The campaign enters eight songs across eight categories, with Sachdev credited as the submitter for the album under Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media, per Times Now's reporting. The pushed tracks — "Phir Se," "Jaan Se Guzarte Hai," "Kanhaiyya," "Aari Aari," "Jaiye Sajana," "Destiny – Mann Atkeya," "Vaari Jaavan" and "Hum Pyaar Karne Wale".

Context & Background

Dhurandhar and Dhurandhar: The Revenge are the two-part Hindi-language spy thrillers written, directed and produced by Aditya Dhar and backed by Jio Studios and B62 Studios. The first film released on December 5, 2025; the second on March 19, 2026. They follow an undercover Indian intelligence agent — Jaskirat Singh Rangi, played by Ranveer Singh, who assumes the identity of Hamza Ali Mazari — as he infiltrates criminal syndicates and political power structures in Karachi's Lyari district to dismantle a terror network targeting India.

https://x.com/TSeries/status/2108547700761546896

The ensemble cast includes Sanjay Dutt, Akshaye Khanna, R. Madhavan, Arjun Rampal and Sara Arjun. Made back-to-back on a reported joint budget of ₹255 crore, the duology grossed over ₹3,200 crore, making it the second-highest-grossing Indian film franchise of all time.

The music has been central to the franchise's identity from the start. The first film's soundtrack became the first Bollywood album to have every track chart simultaneously within Spotify's Global Top 200. For The Revenge, Sachdev expanded the album to 14 tracks, released on T-Series in March 2026, featuring vocals from Arijit Singh, Jasmine Sandlas, Jyoti Nooran and Jubin Nautiyal

"For us, the two films were one long sonic journey."

— Shashwat Sachdev, composer, in an interview with Moneycontrol

The Grammy consideration race works as a funnel. Recording Academy members and labels submit recordings; screening committees verify eligibility and category placement; voting members then vote on ballots to select nominees, before final-round voting chooses winners. A submission guarantees nothing beyond a place in the pool — most entries do not advance.

Impact & Analysis

The Grammy play arrives with a notable backstory. The Film Federation of India jury snubbed Dhurandhar for India's official Oscar submission slot — a decision the Inshorts report explicitly contrasts with the new Grammy push. With the Academy Awards route closed, the music campaign is the franchise's alternate bid for institutional recognition abroad.

As a strategy, the eight-song, eight-category spread is a classic volume play: more ballot lines raise the statistical odds that at least one track catches a voter's ear. The Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media category rewards albums assembled for film or television; a Hindi-language contender there would be a genuine anomaly.

The campaign also reflects how Indian film music now travels. The album spans qawwali-adjacent textures, rap verses and Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan's legacy material, designed to function as one connected score rather than a collection of singles — which is what a soundtrack category rewards.

Diaspora Angle

Diaspora audiences have a direct stake in this campaign. Dhurandhar became the highest-grossing Hindi film of all time in North America and set new benchmarks in Canada and Australia, per Pinkvilla. A Grammy shortlist spot would be recognition for the diaspora listeners who put the album on the map. With eight songs in the race, diaspora playlists — from "Phir Se" to "Aari Aari" — are already the campaign's unofficial ground game.

What's Next

The Recording Academy will now screen the submissions for eligibility and category placement, after which voting members receive ballots. The nomination shortlist is expected later this year; until then, the eight entered songs sit in the pool with thousands of other submissions. The campaign's real test is whether Academy voters, most of whom have never seen the film, find the music compelling enough to vote for it cold.
